key_insight: Modality Forcing shows that a single text-to-image diffusion transformer can be post-trained to generate both images and depth maps, using sparse depth supervision instead of expensive dense depth data. This makes spatially aware generation much more scalable and practical.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of teaching generative models geometric understanding—like perspective and relative scale—without requiring large amounts of dense depth annotation or complicated training pipelines.
method: Start from a pretrained text-to-image DiT with strong spatial priors.
Apply a simple post-training recipe called Modality Forcing to jointly learn image and depth generation.
Use sparse depth data rather than dense depth supervision to scale training more efficiently.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a simpler path to add 3D-aware spatial reasoning to generative models without expensive labeling or complex adaptation methods. It could improve scene synthesis, depth estimation, and downstream spatial understanding tasks.

paper_title: Modality Forcing for Scalable Spatial Generation
paper_authors: Bardienus Pieter Duisterhof, Deva Ramanan, Jeffrey Ichnowski, Justin Johnson, Keunhong Park
